note: Controlled model mutation only. Every engineering edit is a typed, normalised, validated, revisioned and auditable AuthoringCommand. There is no generic setter, no path-based write, no in-place mutation of a canonical model, and no silent auto-save.
runtime_boundary_note: RUNTIME IS EPHEMERAL. ENGINEERING MODEL IS IMMUTABLE. Phase 4 runtime state has no write path into the engineering model and Phase 5 does not create one. Authoring is a separate subsystem reached only through an explicit authoring transaction; a runtime action carrying a model-write intent is still refused with RUNTIME_MODEL_WRITE_ATTEMPT.
validation_note: A valid authoring transaction means the data model is structurally coherent. It does NOT mean code compliant, safe, structurally adequate, MEP adequate or fire compliant. No authoring result is a compliance statement.
no_autofix_note: No coordination clash is auto-fixed. No MEP is auto-rerouted. No structure is auto-redesigned. No code-required element is auto-added. No code-compliance decision mutates geometry. Authoring reports facts and refuses what it cannot do; it never silently repairs a model.
transaction_transitions_note: DRAFT can never reach COMMITTED directly. Preview, validation and an explicit ready state stand between a draft and any change to the canonical model.
declared_not_implemented_note: These command types exist in the vocabulary so discipline ownership is expressed rather than implied, but no structural, MEP or fire/life-safety authoring is implemented in this phase. Submitting one is refused with COMMAND_NOT_IMPLEMENTED. It is never silently ignored and never silently rewritten into an architectural edit.
forbidden_command_note: There is no arbitrary path-based write and no free-form mutation payload. A command naming one of these types is refused with COMMAND_NOT_ALLOWED.
discipline_note: A command may only write inside the model region its declared discipline owns. An architectural command that would alter a structural, MEP or fire/life-safety record is refused with AUTHORING_SCOPE_VIOLATION rather than allowed to reach across disciplines.
ai_boundary_note: AI may PROPOSE a command. A proposal is never a commit. An AI-sourced command passes through the identical schema, normaliser, validator, revision guard and preview as a user command, and additionally requires an explicit confirmation token before it may be committed. There is no privileged AI write path.
actor_note: There is no authentication in this phase. actor_id is null unless an authenticated identity is supplied by the caller. No user, role or permission is fabricated.
constraint_note: A constraint is part of the command contract and is enforced by the validator. A negative instruction such as 'move the door but do not change the room size' is carried as must_not_change and is never silently violated.
hosted_strategy_note: When a wall carrying doors or windows moves, the strategy must be stated by the caller. There is no default: silently choosing one would decide an engineering question on the user's behalf. A missing strategy is refused with HOSTED_STRATEGY_REQUIRED.
editability_note: Not every displayed property is editable. A DERIVED value is computed and can only change by editing its source. A DISPLAY_ONLY value is presentation and never engineering data. An UNKNOWN value is not stated by the source and is not invented.
derived_id_namespace_note: An identifier in a derived namespace names a projection, not a semantic source. It is refused as an authoring target with INVALID_TARGET so a runtime obstacle, a coordination finding or a visual object can never be edited as if it were engineering content. The one place a visual identifier is accepted is PROMOTE_VISUAL_OBJECT, where it is recorded as provenance and never resolved as a target.
read_only_element_note: A derived element is edited by editing the semantic source it was derived from, never directly. A compiled wall is a projection of the space rectangles that generate it; a runtime obstacle is a projection of a visual object; a coordination finding is a projection of geometry.
issue_code_note: These are authoring and model-integrity codes. None of them is a code violation, a compliance finding or a safety judgement.
commit_policy_note: A model-integrity ERROR always rejects the commit. A WARNING — for example a coordination finding that appeared or disappeared — does not reject the commit by itself, but under the declared default policy it must be acknowledged explicitly by the caller. The policy is stated here rather than hidden in code, and ALLOW_SILENTLY is available only if a caller chooses it deliberately.
confirmation_note: A destructive command, or any command whose dependency report is non-empty, requires an explicit confirmation token equal to the transaction's computed confirmation digest. A harmless preview never requires confirmation.
security_note: Authoring input is untrusted. Prototype-pollution keys, script payloads, javascript: URLs, non-finite numbers, absurd coordinates, oversized payloads and over-nested structures are refused. No eval, no exec and no new Function is used anywhere in the authoring engine.
dependency_graph_note: STRUCTURE, MEP and FLS are absent from architectural entries on purpose: an architectural edit never rebuilds or moves a structural, MEP or fire/life-safety element. Those disciplines appear only through COORDINATION, which reports the geometric consequence factually without changing them. DELETE_DOOR lists FLS because a fire/life-safety record may reference the deleted door — that reference is reported, never retargeted.
determinism_note: No timestamp, no random value, no UUID and no wall-clock reading enters a command hash, a revision id or a generated element id. The same base model plus the same normalised command always yields a byte-identical candidate model and the same new model hash. created_at is recorded for audit but is excluded from every identity hash.
audit_note: The audit log records what changed and who or what asked for it. It never records a secret, a token, an API key or any AI chain-of-thought.
snap_note: Snapping is a user-authoring aid applied to command parameters before normalisation. The edit grid is NOT a structural grid and is never linked to one unless a caller states that link explicitly. Only NONE and GRID are implemented in this phase; the remaining types are declared so the architecture is stated rather than improvised later.
gizmo_note: A transform handle produces a typed domain command, never a direct mesh transform. Walls, doors and windows are not generic meshes and may not be scaled arbitrarily; ROTATE and SCALE are exposed only where they carry a domain meaning, which in this phase is the building transform alone.
promotion_note: A visual-only object never becomes engineering content implicitly. Converting one requires the explicit PROMOTE_VISUAL_OBJECT command carrying a target semantic kind, properties and provenance. There is no automatic promotion path.
lock_note: A locked element cannot be the target of a mutating command. Locks are semantic, not a permission system: there are no users and no roles in this phase.
nl_pipeline_note: Natural language never reaches the model directly. Every stage is explicit, and the pipeline stops at a proposal: a human confirmation is required between PREVIEW and COMMIT.
coordination_note: A preview reports how coordination findings change. It never resolves one. RESOLVED_BY_CHANGE means a finding is no longer produced by the candidate geometry; it does not mean the underlying issue was fixed on purpose or correctly.
compliance_note: Egress, navigation and distance results shown in a preview are geometric facts about the candidate model. compliance stays NOT_EVALUATED. No rule result is carried forward across a geometry change; a committed change invalidates affected rule-result snapshots by model hash and explicit re-evaluation remains required.
